faqs.q: How does your contingency model work?
faqs.a: You pay nothing upfront. Our compensation is a negotiated percentage of the actual cash we recover from claims that were previously written off or languishing past 90+ days. If we recover nothing, you owe nothing.

faqs.q: Can you recover claims that payers denied for 'Timely Filing Exceeded'?
faqs.a: Yes. In the majority of timely filing denials, original electronic transmission records (EDI 277 CA acceptances) exist that prove the initial submission occurred within the payer's window. We obtain clearinghouse logs to overturn these wrongful denials.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a claim rejection and a claim denial?
faqs.a: A rejection occurs at the clearinghouse before the payer processes the claim (e.g. invalid member ID format). A denial happens after the payer adjudicates the claim and decides not to pay. Rejections can be fixed instantly; denials require formal appeals.

faqs.q: How quickly do you respond when a high-dollar denial lands?
faqs.a: Our standard service level agreement (SLA) requires every claim denial to be reviewed and assigned to an appeals specialist within 24 to 48 business hours.

faqs.q: How long does medical credentialing typically take in the US?
faqs.a: Commercial payers typically take 90 to 120 days, while Medicare takes 45 to 60 days via PECOS. Our proactive follow-up eliminates administrative stalling, shortening overall turnaround times significantly.

faqs.q: Can we bill retroactively for services rendered while waiting for credentialing?
faqs.a: Medicare allows up to 30 days of retrospective billing from the date the application was submitted. Some commercial payers honor backdating if negotiated upfront. We guide you on the exact rules for your state and payer mix.
